max: Noticed a spike in streaming latency when we tried larger continuous-batching windows last night. Flush cadence seems off — clients see long pauses then bursts. Anyone else?
perf-bot: Deploy 2026-02-10T03:12Z - streaming pipeline - 5.2% p99 increase vs baseline. Stack: runtime v1.14.3, kernels: auto
dana: I saw profiling — partial-decode scheduling is waiting for full batch completion before emitting chunks. That would explain pause+burst.
arjun: That's the batch formation policy. We currently do strict pack by token budget then flush when either budget hit or timer expires.
elaine: Could be KV cache variance too. Some requests have cache hits so decode token counts differ, leading to stragglers. We should consider per-request token-budget instead of per-batch.
yuki: Proposed quick experiment: prioritize streaming requests in the queue (higher priority) so they form smaller batches and get earlier partial-decode scheduling. Also reduce per-batch token target for streaming-tagged calls.
max: Can we toggle kernel selection to prefer low-latency kernels for small partial-decode batches? Might trade throughput.
arjun: We can force select kernels with --kernel-mode=latency for streaming. Profiling suggests kernel selection add ~0.8ms per call for small batches.
perf-bot: perf snapshot: partial-decode emit wait: mean 45ms -> 120ms after change; kernel selection overhead 0.8ms; scheduling stalls due to queue head-of-line blocking 60ms.
dana: Here's a snippet of heuristic config I want to try:
```
batching:
  mode: continuous
  target_token_budget: 128 # per-batch tokens
  per_request_token_cap: 32 # upper bound so no single req blocks
  streaming_priority: high
  emit_policy: partial_decode_on_slot # emit as soon as partial decode ready
  flush_timer_ms: 12
```
elaine: If we do partial_decode_on_slot we must ensure partial decodes use KV cache correctly (don't evict). Also need to avoid double-decode when fallback kernel swapped.
arjun: Another angle: make the queue policy non-FIFO for streaming: allow x slots reserved for 'streaming' to prevent big non-streaming requests starving.
yuki: We should run 1hr A/B with --kernel-mode=latency + per_request_token_cap=32. Instrument: per-token latency, time-to-first-byte, p50/p90/p99 for streaming.
max: Also add tracing for partial-decode scheduling points and kernel selection decisions. Add a tag to logs: scheduling_event={queued,slot_assigned,decode_started,emit}
perf-bot: Started experiment branch: ci/streaming-batch-tune-17682. Running on canary pool.
dana: Quick note: watch out for throughput drop. If we prioritize streaming too much we might increase cost for batch queries.
elaine: Agreed. Keep autoscaler thresholds. For the canary, limit traffic to 10% and run for 30m.
max: SGTM. I'll set up the experiment and share initial numbers in this thread.
